LESSON: BELIEF IN THE LAST DAY HELLFIRE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.1: Belief in the Last Day Hellfire

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Belief in the Last Day Hellfire. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important for Muslims to believe in the Last Day?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the events of the Last Day for accountability

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BELIEF IN THE LAST DAY HELLFIRE
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Belief in the Last Day Hellfire helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BELIEF IN THE LAST DAY HELLFIRE
Study Belief in the Last Day Hellfire like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the events of the Last Day for accountability

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the events of the Last Day for accountability. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the events of the Last Day for accountability.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Belief in the Last Day Hellfire” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the events of the Last Day for accountability. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Belief in the Last Day Hellfire is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Belief in the Last Day Hellfire” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the events of the Last Day for accountability)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Belief in the Last Day Hellfire to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the events of the Last Day for accountability.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Belief in the Last Day Hellfire from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Belief in the Last Day Hellfire: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Belief in the Last Day Hellfire?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important for Muslims to believe in the Last Day?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Belief in the Last Day Hellfire means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the events of the Last Day for accountability.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
